items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: I remember one time... the producer of the show had Panassie Pernasie... I remember Mezzrow was with him, had come with him to the show... That was the only time I saw them.

ctx.x: That's unfortunate. It seemed to me and I may be wrong, but it seemed to me that he was in New York at the time that Mezzrow formed that band and went into that New York spot, that integrated band.

I remember one time, the only time I think he came, unless I am mistaken. I was playing with Benny Goodman and the producer of the show had Panassie Pernasie, John Hammond Panassie. I think, was not the producer -- he got Pernasian to talk and I remember Mezzrow was with him, had come with him to the show.

That was the only time I saw them. We went out that night, went to a little restaurant in the Village, and I remember that a corny recording of Tiger Rag was being played on the Musak, they had in the restaurant, and we were all laughing, it was a satire on jazz, it was so bad, and Panassie Pernasian, he thought it was excellent, so I began to realize that he might not have known too much about jazz.

items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Not critics, I am sorry to say, with the exception perhaps of a few, such as you and Stanley Dance, Leonard Feather.

ctx.x: I had ever heard, and of course, Sid Catlett and Dave were considered the tops of their times.

Bear in mind that Dave Tough influenced people like the so-called modern drummers. Now, we in jazz, we musicians in jazz do not use categories. We do not put people into categories and I will go into that in a few minutes. We don't call a man a modern drummer or an avant garde drummer or a dixieland drummer. A man can either play or he cannot. This is what it's about and only musicians know this. Not critics, I am sorry to say, with the exception perhaps of a few, such as you and Stanley Dance, Leonard Feather.…

Say that musicians never called the music jazz, but they knew what they were hearing and what they were feeling. It was the only kind of music they could find wherein they could express their feelings, because they worked all day in studios or theatres and all night in night- clubs, playing dance music or playing other people's acts, but why did they want to play this kind of music? Because they had a chance to express what they felt about music.
